messages:
maria: Quick thread — we ran into a weird edge case in tonight's load test where Frontdoor failed over mid-stream and the downstream proxy closed the TCP connection. client saw a partial response with no resume token.
ashok: Ugh. Was that the canary region or main?
ben: Canary. Repro steps: long streaming response (~120s), then we flip route to a fallback region with a 1s drain. The upstream sends EOF, downstream aborts, client gets truncated body. No retry because request wasn't marked idempotent.
maria: The conversation: should Frontdoor be responsible for inserting a resume token before initiating failover, or should the upstream runtime emit it proactively?
sam: I'm leaning upstream. Runtime has model-level knowledge to produce safe checkpoints (kv boundaries). Frontdoor can't guess safe cut points.
ashok: Agree on safe cut points, but what about fast failover scenarios where runtime is unreachable? Frontdoor could produce a lightweight opaque checkpoint (hash of bytes) to enable partial replays if runtime supports reconciling by offset.
eva: That adds coupling. If Frontdoor starts owning token generation, now it needs to understand model framing. Nightmare for future models.
ben: Tradeoff: if we require runtime to always produce resume markers at periodic safe points (e.g., every 2s or N tokens), we increase latency slightly but keep separation of concerns.
maria: Also consider cost: adding frequent checkpoints increases response size and CPU. Heavy workloads will feel it.
sam: Could we do a hybrid: runtime emits semantic checkpoints when safe; Frontdoor injects a minimal opaque continuation header (not semantic) that says "last-byte-offset" + hash. On reattach, runtime verifies hash. If runtime can't verify, fall back to full restart.
ashok: That seems pragmatic. But we need an explicit failure contract: if verification fails, Frontdoor should decide whether to re-route to original runtime (if healthy) or return 502. We can't silently drop state.
eva: Also need to consider retries for non-idempotent requests. If resume is impossible and we retry, side effects could be duplicated. We need a side-effect marker for routes that mutate externally (webhooks, DB writes).
ben: Proposal: augment call metadata with three flags: "resume_capable" (bool), "semantic_checkpointing" (bool), "side_effects" (enum: none/visible/managed). Frontdoor uses those to decide: graceful handoff -> attach continuation header; hard failover -> if resume_capable && semantic_checkpointing then attempt transparent reconnect; else if side_effects==none then retry; else return error.
maria: From impl perspective: gateway adds header: X-Resume-Opaque: base64(offset|hash). Runtime exposes API to verify and accept continuation via HTTP endpoint /_resume_validate. Small handshake: POST with header, returns 200 if accepted else 409.
sam: We should define handshake TTL and backoff. Also instrument counts: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_latency in console.
ashok: Observability is key. Add tracing spans: frontdoor.resume.validate and frontdoor.resume.attach.
eva: Security: continuation header must be signed with per-customer HMAC key (from KMS) to avoid cross-tenant replay.
ben: Good call. For Dedicated/Private deployments, runtime can opt into local signing keys. Hosted uses Redwood KMS.
maria: Quick question: how do we treat streaming trailers? If we resume, trailers might already have been sent. We need to ensure trailers are idempotent or rendered only at final completion.
sam: Let's enforce a rule: trailers are only emitted on a final completion signal. Interim checkpoints must not emit final-status trailers. Runtime change required.
ashok: Edge case: third-party clients that rely on trailers for status. We'll need a migration doc and compatibility mode: if client opts into legacy trailers, frontdoor disables resume for that route.
eva: Ops: create rollout plan: 1) runtime checkpoint API + semantic markers, 2) frontdoor continuation header (opt-in per route), 3) observability + signing, 4) canary enabled, 5) default off for legacy routes.
ben: I'll sketch an RFC and include sequence diagrams + error codes (409 validation failed, 428 resume required but not possible, 502 fallback fail).
ci-bot: Deploy note: remember to add feature flag "resume-handoff" behind config.
maria: Thanks. Can we sync tomorrow 10:30 to finalize API surfaces?
eva: I'll join and bring a short compatibility matrix.
sam: I'll prototype the /_resume_validate handshake this week.
ben: I'll add the console metrics hooks.
maria: Awesome. For the RFC title: "frontdoor resume handoff: opaque continuation header and runtime validation" (will not be used as filename). :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Reminder: link to testing checklist: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/resume-handoff-checklist
maria: End thread.
